_doc: ui fragment (act 06, the workspace window). Everything lives in the agent panel on the right of the window, so every UI sound is panned right (0.6 = x 1570 px, the middle of the step rows at 1360-1780). Levels are RELATIVE to the music peaks, which are about -3..-6 dBFS premaster (measured on the temp score): UI peaks sit 12-15 dB under them (keys -24 each, about -18 as a 40/s burst; click -18; step notes -17), Task 6 balances the buses. Cues: act06:key:1..55 (one per prompt character, 25 ms apart from 66.0 s), act06:step:1..5 (70.0 71.0 72.0 73.0 74.5), act06:word:1 (ASK, 66.0: the panel starts to lift and the prompt starts to type; the click sits 30 ms before it). Nothing here sounds the four act-06 word pops or the 75.5 collapse whoosh (transitions / music own those).

ui.keys._doc: laptop typing (Mixkit 2531, 19.6 s of single presses). 20 clean takes picked from the --dump of the default slicer (head below -40 dB, tail below -38 dB, attack <= 7 ms, 0.085-0.141 s long, spread over the file so the takes come from different keys). len 0.07 + 30 ms fade keeps each take short: at 25 ms per character up to 3 takes overlap, long tails would turn it to mush. The recording's own bottom-out thock is kept; HP 180 Hz takes the desk rumble off, LP 9 kHz takes the paper-thin top that would be harsh at 40 keys per second.

ui.click._doc: Mixkit 1116 'Single classic click': click + release, attack at 0.112 s. The panel is clicked into focus right before the lift. LP 6.5 kHz (its centre of gravity is 7 kHz: it would cut through the keys).

_notify_doc: step-done notifications: real Iowa crotale notes (realness 0.96+), not Mixkit 3109 (a weak match for 'soft bell chime', and its tail rings G6, outside D major). The five steps climb the D-major tones the crotales have: D6 E6 F#6 A6 on steps 1-4 (progress going up), and the last step (the summary card) lands on D6 + A6 together, an open fifth that closes on the tonic. 1.1 s trim, 0.6 s fade; LP 4.2 kHz takes the metal strike off so it reads as a soft ding, HP 900 Hz. Nowhere near the logo's A4 / D5 / F#5 at 58-59 s (12 s away, an octave higher or more).
